name: Cabedelo (Viana do Castelo)
notes: Long dune-backed beach on the south bank of the Lima mouth, best by the breakwater; a reference kite and windsurf spot when the summer north wind blows.

name: Aguçadoura
notes: Exposed, consistent beach break that is usually uncrowded and works through the tide in offshore easterlies.

name: Azurara
notes: Long sandy beach split by old groynes that shape the peaks, sheltered from north wind by the Vila do Conde jetty.

name: Matosinhos
notes: Wide city beach sheltered by the Leixões harbour wall, with gentle waves that make it the main learning spot near Porto.

name: Espinho
notes: Groyne-divided town beach whose Baía peak hosts national and WSL junior events; powerful and hollow when the banks are good.

name: Praia da Barra
notes: Beach just south of the Aveiro harbour jetty with several peaks; rarely flat and the busiest surf spot of the Aveiro coast.

name: Buarcos
notes: Right-hand point that wraps along Buarcos bay, sheltered from north wind; rides of a few hundred metres on a big clean swell.

name: Cabedelo (Figueira da Foz)
notes: Long right on the south side of the Mondego mouth, protected from north wind by the breakwater; historic national and international contest venue.

name: Praia do Norte (Nazaré)
notes: Big-wave beach focused by the Nazaré submarine canyon; giant days are tow-in territory and the shorebreak is deadly.

name: Lagoa de Óbidos
notes: Shallow lagoon behind Foz do Arelho; flat-water kite and windsurf spot in the summer north wind.

name: Lagide
notes: Flat reef at the east end of Baleal bay with lefts and rights; works in westerly and southerly wind when the north coast is blown out.

name: Baleal
notes: Curved bay between Peniche and the Baleal tombolo with many peaks; the main learning area of Peniche and offshore in southerly winds.

name: Molhe Leste
notes: Right-hand sandbar against the east breakwater of Peniche harbour; a softer option next to Supertubos on southwest swell.

name: Supertubos
notes: Hollow, shallow sandbar barrels a short walk from Peniche harbour; venue of the WSL Championship Tour event.

name: São Lourenço
notes: Northernmost wave of the Ericeira surfing reserve: a heavy right over rock in front of a sandy bay, best on big northwest swell.

name: Coxos
notes: Hollow, powerful right over a rock shelf in a small cove; one of the most demanding waves of the Ericeira reserve.

name: Ribeira d'Ilhas
notes: Long right-hand point over rock and cobble at the heart of the Ericeira reserve; regular venue of WSL events.

name: Pedra Branca
notes: Shallow left-hand reef just north of Ericeira town, hollow and fast on west to northwest swell.

name: Foz do Lizandro
notes: Sandy river-mouth beach south of Ericeira; the go-to learning spot of the area at mid to high tide.

name: Praia Grande (Sintra)
notes: Exposed beach below the Sintra hills; long-standing venue of international bodyboard events with powerful waves.

name: Guincho
notes: Exposed beach west of Cascais with year-round surf and a strong summer north wind that makes it a reference kite and windsurf spot.

name: Carcavelos
notes: Long beach of the Cascais line, ten minutes from Lisbon; hollow sandbars on west to southwest swell and very crowded.

name: Costa da Caparica
notes: Groyne-divided town beaches where peaks form beside the rock jetties; busy learning and surf school area.

name: Lagoa de Albufeira
notes: Sheltered lagoon behind the Albufeira bar; flat-water kite and windsurf spot in the summer northerly.

name: São Torpes
notes: Beach south of Sines port, warmed by the power-station outfall; sheltered from north wind and a winter alternative when the coast is big.

name: Malhão
notes: Long exposed beach north of Milfontes with multiple peaks; one of the most consistent breaks of the Alentejo coast.

name: Odeceixe
notes: Beach at the Seixe river mouth on the Alentejo–Algarve border; sandbars shaped by the river make it a popular learning spot.

name: Arrifana
notes: Cliff-ringed bay sheltered from north wind, with a beach break for learners and a right point over rock at its northern end.

name: Bordeira
notes: Wide, fully exposed beach at Carrapateira with a river-mouth sandbar; powerful and consistent.

name: Amado
notes: Consistent beach break south of Carrapateira with several peaks and many surf schools; contest venue that holds a big swell.

name: Beliche
notes: Cliff-backed cove inside Cape St Vincent, sheltered from north wind and good when the west coast is too big or windy.

name: Tonel
notes: Exposed beach under the Sagres fortress, the most consistent spot of the Sagres area with peaks across the tide.

name: Zavial
notes: Right-hand point and beach on the south coast west of Salema; comes alive on winter southwest swells with northerly wind.

name: Praia da Luz
notes: Sheltered south-coast bay that wakes up on winter southwest swells; a reef in front of Rocha Negra suits better surfers.

name: Meia Praia
notes: Long sandy bay east of Lagos with gentle south-swell waves for learners and good kite conditions in onshore afternoon breezes.

name: Praia da Rocha
notes: Wide beach west of the Portimão jetty that picks up more south and southwest swell than most of the south Algarve.

name: Praia de Faro
notes: Barrier-island beach of the Ria Formosa near Faro airport; small southwest-swell waves for beginners.

name: Jardim do Mar
notes: Long, powerful right-hand point over boulders below the village of the same name; Madeira's flagship big-wave spot.

name: Paul do Mar
notes: Heavy, hollow right over volcanic boulders at the fishing village of Paul do Mar; handles big winter swells.

name: Lugar de Baixo
notes: Fast, hollow boulder-reef wave near Ponta do Sol on the island's south coast.

name: Porto da Cruz
notes: Pebble beach on the north-east coast promoted by Madeira's surf club as the island's safest place to learn.

name: São Vicente
notes: Black-sand and boulder beach at Fajã da Areia on the north coast, home of the São Vicente surf club and suited to intermediates.
